sourceRefs.locator: “Various treatments”, “A temporary solution” and “Problem solved”, figs 2, 4–9: four animal heads and two sledge pulls, the two specially made aquariums commissioned in 1912, the wartime loss, Jørgen Eriksen’s copy and Annemor Rosenqvist’s treatment before the 1957 exhibition.

“Conservation”, “Alum treatment” and “Re-construction” explain groundwater and low oxygen, pressure damage, the risk of shrinkage, drying of better-preserved oak, and the contrasting treatment of fragile carvings.
